headline: Selling Was Broad and Deep on Wednesday; Oil Fears and Global Tensions Set the Tone for Thursday's Open
body_html:
Markets head into Thursday's session carrying the weight of a punishing Wednesday. Of 544 names in our universe, just 135 finished higher while 407 closed lower — a lopsided result that spanned nearly every corner of the market. Homebuilders led the damage with a 3.0% sector decline, followed by Materials off 2.42% and Industrials down 2.1%. Healthcare was the lone relatively sheltered ground, slipping only 0.23%.

The dominant pre-market narrative belongs to crude oil. Houthi forces claimed a ballistic missile strike on Riyadh's airport overnight, and data tracking the Strait of Hormuz shows transit volumes at their lowest level in more than two months following a string of shipping attacks. Oil prices jumped in response, keeping energy supply risk front and center as Thursday's session approaches. That dynamic reinforces Wednesday's underperformance in Energy, which shed 1.18%, and suggests commodity-linked names will remain volatile at the open.

On the corporate side, Samsung's forecast of a record third-quarter profit — powered by artificial intelligence demand — offers a constructive signal for the semiconductor complex ahead of the bell. Micron was Wednesday's standout in that space, gaining 4.06%, while Glaukos and Progyny paced healthcare with advances of 6.55% and 6.33% respectively. Traders will watch whether those pockets of strength can hold as geopolitical pressure persists.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Traffic Dries Up as Shipping Attacks Escalate
briefs.body: Vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen to their lowest level in more than two months, according to tracking data, following a renewed wave of attacks in the region. The constriction adds a tangible supply-risk premium to crude prices heading into Thursday and puts energy-exposed equities on watch at the open.

briefs.headline: Houthis Claim Strike on Saudi Capital's Airport
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthi movement said it launched a ballistic missile at Riyadh's airport, the latest in a series of strikes targeting Gulf infrastructure. The attack follows reports that Syria is weighing involvement in the Yemen conflict after earlier Houthi fire hit Saudi airport facilities, deepening regional instability.

briefs.headline: Samsung's AI-Driven Profit Forecast Lifts Chip Sentiment
briefs.body: Samsung projected a record third-quarter profit of $80 billion, citing surging demand tied to the artificial intelligence build-out. The guidance provides a positive backdrop for semiconductor names Thursday morning, a sector that shed 1.83% on Wednesday but saw Micron buck the trend with a 4.06% gain.

briefs.headline: Materials Stocks Among Wednesday's Hardest Hit
briefs.body: The Materials sector fell 2.42% on Wednesday, with Worthington Steel dropping 6.89% and Materion sliding 6.87% to rank among the session's steepest decliners. The dual selloff in steel and advanced-materials names reflects broader anxiety over global industrial demand and supply-chain uncertainty.

briefs.headline: Russia-China Hypersonic Threat Spurs Space-Defense Debate
briefs.body: A satellite industry executive cited growing hypersonic missile capabilities from Russia and China as a key driver of demand for space-based defense architecture. The remarks add a commercial dimension to an accelerating geopolitical arms dynamic that investors in the defense and satellite sectors will be monitoring closely.

briefs.headline: NFL Urges Supreme Court to Let States Govern Prediction Markets
briefs.body: The National Football League submitted arguments to the Supreme Court contending that sports-event prediction markets constitute gambling and should fall under state regulatory authority rather than federal commodity rules. The filing escalates a legal battle that carries significant implications for platforms operating event-contract trading products.
